messages:
jamal: quick question — contractor needs to monitor ingestion job statuses across a handful of projects, but must NOT be able to see request payloads / PII in logs. what's the least-privileged approach here?

maria: don't give org-level Viewer. really depends on what 'monitor' means: job state + metadata vs full log access. two safe patterns: 1) create a project-scoped custom role that only surfaces metadata (if that data exists separately), or 2) export logs to a sanitized sink (bigquery) and grant read only to the sanitized dataset. IAM alone can't do field-level redaction.

eli: +1. roles/logging.viewer will let them read textPayload — so that would leak PII if payloads are there. if you need to stick with logging, do an export sink and run a redact step (cloud function/dataflow) to strip fields before storing. then give them BigQuery read on that sanitized table.

ryan: if they only need job status, consider a tiny internal read-only service that surfaces statuses (no payloads) and grant them access to that. much easier to reason about than custom logging perms.

maria: example of a minimal custom role (project scope) — still a warning: logging permission will expose raw entries if present:

```
# create a narrow role in the project
gcloud iam roles create jobViewer --project=my-project \
  --title="Job Viewer (limited)" \
  --permissions=cloudresourcemanager.projects.get,cloudresourcemanager.projects.list,logging.logEntries.list,ml.jobs.get \
  --stage=GA

# bind to the contractor (replace with group/service account)
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding my-project \
  --member='user:contractor@example.com' --role='projects/my-project/roles/jobViewer'
```

But note: `logging.logEntries.list` will surface textPayload. if that's a no-go, use a sanitized export instead.

jamal: got it. so the recommended path is: export logs -> redact on ingest -> store sanitized table -> grant BigQuery read. for short-term testing can we do a time-limited grant instead of permanent role?

sec-bot: Reminder: contractors require an access request in #access-requests: include projects, justification, duration (max 30 days), and approvers. Use a service account with workload identity where possible.

maria: yes. for contractors we prefer: service account + limited roles + TTL. security will only approve after we see the redaction plan or a sanitized dataset. i'll approve a 24h test window for the contractor once the pipeline is sketched.

jamal: perfect — i'll draft the access request and a short design for the redaction pipeline (fields to remove, retention, who owns the sink). thanks everyone :thumbsup:
